text: Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Premier League fixture between Luton Town and Arsenal at Kenilworth Road.
Arsenal have won three Premier League games in a row to open up a two-point lead on Liverpool and a three-point advantage on reigning champions Manchester City.
With those two sides not in action today, Mikel Arteta's side can give themselves a little breathing space at the summit for the time being.
Luton's sole focus is on staying in the top flight following their promotion from the Championship last season.
Rob Edwards' men lost 3-1 away to Brentford at the weekend, but they have drawn with Liverpool and beaten Crystal Palace in their past two home matches.
They enter this game two points clear of the relegation zone.
Edwards has made four changes to the Luton XI from their loss at Brentford three days ago.
Brown has scored in his last two matches as a substitute and is handed a start in attack, while Adebayo is also restored to the frontline, with Ogbene and Morris dropping down to the bench.
Former Tottenham winger Townsend and fit-again Doughty are the other two recalled players, taking the places of Chong and injured skipper Tom Lockyer, who is not in the squad.
Arsenal show three changes from their 2-1 win over Wolves on Saturday.
Two of those alterations come in defence - or more specifically at full-back - as White and Kiwior replace Zinchenko and Takehiro Tomiyasu, the latter of whom is not in the squad.
Havertz also returns to the starting line-up in place of the benched Trossard.
Academy product Walters, yet to make his senior debut, is among the defensive cover on the bench.
This is the first meeting between Luton Town and Arsenal in any competition since December 1991, with the Hatters prevailing 1-0 at Kenilworth Road.
They would certainly take a repeat of that today in this tussle between sides with contrasting ambitions for the campaign.
We are now just a few moments away from kick-off.
Arsenal get us up and running at Kenilworth Road! The Gunners are the strong favourites today, but Liverpool dropped two points here not so long ago.
The visitors, as you would expect, have dominated possession in the early stages.
Martinelli shows some great footwork and is wiped out by Townsend close to the touchline for an Arsenal free-kick.
Rice sends the free-kick into a dangerous zone around the penalty spot, but a Luton player gets it clear.
Barkley feels he is caught when trying to start a counter, but the referee disagrees.
Mengi barges into the back of Martinelli, who goes to ground.
There did not look to be a great deal in it on initial viewing, but the Arsenal physio is on the pitch.
The knee of Mengi went into the back of Martinelli, explaining the Brazilian's discomfort.
After a bit of treatment, the Arsenal forward is back on the field.
Martinelli is straight into the thick of the action after returning to the field, but his cross from the left is overhit.
Luton try to get the ball forward but the attack fizzles out.
Barkley catches Kiwior and in the process further disrupts Arsenal's rhythm.
The visitors have bossed possession early on, but Luton are breaking up play with challenge after challenge - Saka the latest to be taken out.
The Luton backroom staff are frantically pointing something out to Edwards on one of the laptops, presumably tactics related.
The home side have enjoyed a rare spell of possession over the past couple of minutes, but that ends with a foul on Saka.
A quarter of an hour into the contest and we have yet to see any efforts at either end.
Luton boss Edwards will be pleased with how his side have kept Arsenal quiet, even if they have had 67 per cent of the ball.
Brown gets to the byline, only for his cross to get cut out.
Doughty fares no better as Arsenal deal with the second ball into the middle.
Arsenal have not found their rhythm at all, and that is entirely down to Luton.
Kabore goes in hard on Martinelli to concede another free-kick - a perfect example of how the Hatters are managing to frustrate their opponents.
White fails to keep a simple ball under control, not helped by the pressure he is being put under.
Luton have actually been the better side over the past 10 minutes, albeit without creating much of note, a couple of cleared crosses aside.
GOOOAAALLL!!! LUTON 0-1 ARSENAL! A poor pass back to Kaminski is not really dealt with by the goalkeeper, who kicks it out for a throw-in.
Some quick thinking by Jesus from a throw-in has Saka in, and he pulls it back to the penalty spot for Martinelli to tuck away.
One shot, one goal for the visitors!
A lapse in Luton concentration is pounced on by Arsenal - and Saka in particular.
He looks up, spots Martinelli and nicely plays the ball into the path of his team-mate to do the rest.
The Premier League can be brutal at times, as Luton just found out.
They have been the better side overall, but Arsenal find a way through from their first meaningful attack.
Jesus gets a shot away, but it is a simple one for Kaminski to deal with.
Luton get up the other end and win the game's first corner through Brown.
GOOOAAALLL!!! LUTON 1-1 ARSENAL!! An instant response from the hosts! Doughty sends in an outswinging corner and Osho is there to head in, pretty much unmarked, from 10 yards out.
Terrible defending from the visitors, but a decent header from Osho for his first Premier League goal.
Doughty's corner was into a perfect area for Osho to attack.
Luton have made the most of set-piece opportunities this season, this being the latest such example.
SAVE! That Luton goal was a shock to Arsenal's system, having taken the lead against the run of play a few moments beforehand.
Jesus gets a shot away from a tight angle, which Kaminski helps into the side netting for a corner that ultimately comes to nothing.
We certainly have a contest on our hands at Kenilworth Road.
Luton are giving as good as they get so far - they are more than good value for their leveller.
GREAT SAVE! Jesus does well to lay the ball into the path of Martinelli, who connects well with his shot.
Kaminski gets a strong hand to it to deny the Brazilian.
This is better from Arsenal.
Brown scythes down Gabriel and is rightly cautioned by referee Samuel Barrott.
Kabore hits the ball into his own hand when trying to clear it and VAR briefly checks for a penalty, but that was never going to be given.
The visitors are looking a little livelier in the attacking third now.
If they were not aware of it beforehand, this is not going to be a walk in the park for them.
White is frustratingly caught offside, allowing Luton to slow things down.
Arsenal have not won any of their last six Premier League away games when they have conceded at least once (D3 L3), since a 4-2 win at Aston Villa in February.
Saliba goes through Adebayo - that is proving to be a good tussle - and wins his side a free-kick.
Luton have done well to disrupt Arsenal's play again over the past few minutes, just like they were doing when it was at 0-0.
CLOSE! Kaminski is called into action again, this time to push aside Saka's curling effort.
It is a good save, but one you would expect the Luton keeper to make.
Saka is at the heart of every Arsenal attack.
The Arsenal corner is cleared, but replays show that Kabore headed the ball onto his own arm when intervening.
Nobody appeals for a penalty, but something very similar was given in PSG's favour against Newcastle last week.
Barkley goes sliding in on Martinelli to become the second Luton player to receive a booking.
There was no reason for the midfielder to go to ground there.

GOOOAAAALLL!!!! LUTON 1-2 ARSENAL!! The visitors restore their lead through Jesus! Saka and White exchange passes down the right and the latter floats in a delightful ball that is screaming out for Jesus to attack, and he does just that.
Great cross, great header.
White played the ball to Saka, perhaps expecting his more attack-minded team-mate to make something happen.
When the ball was played back to him, though, he picked out Jesus superbly.
Jesus is booked for a foul on Barkley late in the first half.
The Brazilian pleads with the referee, but that one offence is enough to earn him a caution.
Five minutes have been added on at the end of the first half.
Arsenal will feel they are worthy of that lead, having forced Kaminski into a few saves after being pegged back.
Can the hosts respond before half-time?
SHOT! Doughty brings the ball out of the sky brilliantly.
A cross into the box is cut out for a corner, which Saliba gets to.
Luton keep the attack alive and a powerful Mengi drive is right down the throat of Raya.
HALF-TIME: LUTON TOWN 1-2 ARSENAL
Arsenal take a 2-1 lead into half-time thanks to goals from Martinelli and Jesus, either side of an Osho equaliser.
A poor backpass from Brown forced Kaminski to play the ball out for a throw, which culminated in Saka teeing up Martinelli for the opener.
Osho profited from some disappointing defending to power in a leveller five minutes later, only for Jesus to meet White's floated delivery from the right to restore his side's lead.
Luton boss Edwards will be pretty happy with the overall first-half performance from his side.
The hosts did well to disrupt play and keep Arsenal quiet for the majority of the half, although the Gunners did still manage to find a couple of goals.
While there is still just the one goal in it, Town have a chance of taking a point from this game.
The hosts get us back under way at Kenilworth Road.
Neither manager has made any changes to their personnel at half-time.
Luton have started the second half the brighter of the two sides.
Townsend shows some trickery and sends a cross into the box from the right, but it is as simple as you like for Raya to gather under his crossbar.
Doughty does brilliantly to get in between two Arsenal players as he charges into the box from the left.
He looks to pick out a team-mate in the middle, but the delivery is cut out.
From the next attacking wave, Townsend's long-range drive deflects behind.
GOOOOAAAALLL!!! LUTON 2-2 ARSENAL!! Another corner, another goal for Luton! Doughty sends in an in-swinger from the right this time and Adebayo gets above both Rice and Raya to head in.
Poor goalkeeping, that!
Doughty now has two assists for the day.
Arsenal cannot deal with his set-piece deliveries! Raya really should have been doing better to get his hands to that corner.
Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 32 Premier League matches when leading at half-time (W29, D3), dating back to January 2022 against Manchester City (1-2).
Can Luton score another to pull off an almighty upset?
The offside flag goes up to deny Saka in a bit of a chaotic period, but VAR wants to check an earlier incident.
Kiwior is caught by Townsend, possibly on the edge of the box.
Alternatively, it may well be that they are looking at Kiwior catching Townsend on the shin.
Either way, the referee has resumed the game.
Odegaard sends a decent delivery into the box and it is met by Havertz.
He is rather stationary, though, and is unable to guide his header on target.
We are entering the period of the game in which both managers - but mainly Arteta - will be considering a change or two.
Arsenal have not got going at all in this second half.
GOOOAAALLL!!! LUTON 3-2 ARSENAL!! The hosts lead! Townsend decides against shooting and instead plays it back to Barkley towards the left.
The former Everton midfielder steps over the ball and fires an angled drive on target that goes right under the body of Raya.
Yet more terrible goalkeeping!
Townsend was played in by Barkley but did not fancy the shot, so he instead returned it to his team-mate.
Fair play to Barkley because the angle was not on his side, yet he still found the net.
Given the whole goalkeeping narrative at Arsenal, all focus will be on Raya at full-time.
He has been at fault for at least one goal today, possibly even two.

GOOOAAAALLL!!! LUTON 3-3 ARSENAL! What a game!! Jesus is being dragged down by Mengi but retains his balance and flicks the ball into the path of Havertz, who gets his leg to the ball ahead of Kaminski to get Arsenal back on level terms.
This is brilliant centre-forward play from Jesus.
He shows good strength to keep Mengi at bay and then finds Havertz in the middle.
Luton make a triple substitution with an hour played.
Top-scoring striker Morris is on for Adebayo up top in the first of those.
Brown is off and Chong on in central midfield as Edwards freshens up his midfield.
Ogbene for Townsend is the third change made by Luton.
The substitutions are coming thick and fast now.
Kiwior is off and Zinchenko on in the first of Arsenal's changes.
Martinelli has performed well for Arsenal today, but he is replaced by Trossard with around 25 minutes to go.
Ross Barkley's only previous Premier League goal against Arsenal came back in October 2015 in a 2-1 defeat for Everton at Emirates Stadium.
The longest gap (8 years and 42 days) between league goals for a player against the Gunners since Cristiano Ronaldo scored his first against Arsenal in 13 years and 233 days in December 2021.
There has not been a great deal of note happening since Arsenal's equaliser, not helped by the disruption brought about by those five substitutions.
Arsenal, for the first time this half, have a little control.
Arteta's men have scored three times and yet they are still not ahead.
Luton seem a little happier to sit back now, leaving just Morris up top.
Arsenal have plenty of time to find a winner here, but they must be wary of the counter.
Jesus initially gets away from Bell, and the Luton defender has to be careful not to bring down his opponent.
However, Jesus rather comically hits the ball out of play off his own leg.
Arsenal have had seven shots on target to Luton's four.
The hosts' latest effort, via Mpanzu, is well off target from range.
Saka is in a bit of pain after being caught by Bell.
Saka is being targeted constantly now, with Doughty the latest to take him out from behind.
Luton are not afraid to get in their opponents' faces, and it is paying off for now.
Odegaard is picked out by White from a throw but is not really able to do anything with the ball inside the box.
Arsenal are still on top, but they are not exactly creating anything of note.
SAVE! Odegaard gets a shot on target from 20 yards, which is a nice one for Kaminski to keep out down to his right.
The Gunners possibly starting to turn the screw here.
Saka gets a yard on Bell, but the cross is cut out for a corner.
The Arsenal forward sends it under the crossbar, but it is a player in orange who gets on the end of it.
CHANCE! Saka is involved in everything at the moment.
He wins the ball and cuts in between Bell and Morris, before tapping it into the path of Trossard.
The substitute has a small part of the goal to aim for, but his effort deflects over the bar.
Trossard lets the ball run through but the opportunity to get a shot away does not arise.
VAR checks for a possible Osho foul on Saka, but it is not deemed worthy of checking.
Play resumes.
Trossard is finding himself in some great positions.
White's cross is headed on by Havertz and is just out of the reach of Trossard at the back stick to make proper contact.
Around six minutes of normal time remaining and it is Arsenal who are asking all the questions now.
Odegaard plays a free-kick low into the path of Jesus, but he is unable to find a team-mate.
The Gunners certainly looking as though they have a late winner in them, though.
Yet more clever football from Arsenal, and Trossard in particular, but once again the final pass is lacking as Luton win a goal kick.
Ogbene's eyes light up as he finds himself in space down the left, but his cross is horribly overhit.
Arsenal need to be aware of Town's ability to counter.
SAVE! This is superb play from Arsenal.
They work the ball to Zinchenko, who hangs the ball up for Havertz to meet.
It initially looks like being a superb save, but replays show it was actually going over the crossbar.
SHOT! Trossard's first-time effort from 20 yards skims just wide of the post.
Kaminski looked worried as he dived to his left.
Mpanzu is taken off for the closing stages, with Clark brought on in his place.
Giles for Doughty at left wing-back is Luton's fifth and final change.
Saka is still trying his best to make something happen, but he is crowded out on the edge of the Luton box.
This is not quite relentless pressure from Arsenal, but they are certainly knocking on the door.
Six minutes have been added on at the end of this thrilling game at Kenilworth Road.
Arsenal win themselves another corner in the second minute of added time.
Saka delivers and Osho heads away.
Trossard's shot from range is then blocked by Chong.
Luton supporters are urging their side over the line now.
What a massive point this would be in their fight for survival.
White's low cross from the right hits Ogbene for a late Arsenal corner...
Another Arsenal corner comes to nothing.
Luton are standing firm, as Saka's latest cross is not met by one of his team-mates.
We have played the six minutes of added time.
Surely there is not one more late chance for the visitors - or indeed the hosts?

GOOOOAAAALLL!!! LUTON 3-4 ARSENAL!!!! This is incredible!! In the seventh minute of stoppage time, Rice outjumps Osho and heads Odegaard's exquisite cross into the bottom corner to surely win it for Arsenal.

events.action: heads Odegaard exquisite cross into the bottom corner

text: The Gunners have thrown everything at this and have been duly rewarded.
Odegaard did not have much of an angle to work with, but he put the ball into a good area and Rice got above Osho to guide in a late, late winner.
FULL-TIME: LUTON TOWN 3-4 ARSENAL
Arsenal win a thrilling Premier League contest 4-3 at Kenilworth Road to move five points clear at the summit ahead of the chasing pack playing later in the week.
Martinelli and Jesus scored either side of Osho's header to put the visitors ahead at the break, but Adebayo headed home early in the second half to level up.
Barkley put Town in front, only for Havertz to equalise on the hour and Rice to win it right at the very death.

Just how big a result could that be at both ends of the table come the end of the season? Luton now have five days to get this loss out of their system before hosting Manchester City, while Arsenal - who will lead the table regardless going into the weekend - travel to Aston Villa on Saturday.
That concludes our live coverage from Kenilworth Road.
Thanks for joining!
